input.description: In photosynthesis, plants use light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen. In plant cells this occurs in chloroplasts, whose chlorophyll pigments absorb light.

evidence_map.description: In photosynthesis, plants use light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen. In plant cells this occurs in chloroplasts, whose chlorophyll pigments absorb light.
evidence_map.example-source-1:A: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in sugars.
evidence_map.example-source-2:A: Chloroplasts are the organelles in which plant photosynthesis takes place.
evidence_map.example-source-3:A: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light used in photosynthesis.

questions.question: Plants use light energy to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen in this process. Name the process.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis stores energy from light in sugars.

evidence.claim: The process uses light to make sugars from carbon dioxide and water and releases oxygen.

questions.question: In plant cells, these organelles contain light-absorbing pigments and carry out photosynthesis. Name these organelles.
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the sites of photosynthesis in plant cells.

evidence.claim: Chloroplasts contain pigments and are where photosynthesis occurs.

questions.question: This green pigment absorbs light used in photosynthesis. What is the pigment called?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light that supplies energy for photosynthesis.

evidence.claim: Chlorophyll is a green light-absorbing photosynthetic pigment.
